items.title: South Africa seized 5 ancient baobabs bound for Georgia, where 8 Kenyan trees died in a billionaire’s park
items.summary:
For more than three months, five baobab trees estimated to be 200 to 300 years old lay on their sides in a Durban warehouse parking lot, roots and branches hacked back, waiting to be shipped to the Black Sea nation of Georgia. South Africa’s Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE) intercepted the trees on July 17 after their exporter, Pretoria-based Divine Landscapes, could not produce licenses to remove, transport, or export them.

Officials have not named the buyer. But reporting by Daily Maverick traced the trail to the Shekvetili Dendrological Park, a private arboretum on Georgia’s coast founded by billionaire Bidzina Ivanishvili, the country’s former prime minister and the founder of its ruling Georgian Dream party. Ivanishvili has not commented, and Daily Maverick said requests to his lawyer and to Georgia’s embassy in Pretoria went unanswered.

The case tests how far South Africa will go to keep a protected species from becoming a collectible for wealthy buyers abroad. It also left authorities with a practical problem: keeping living evidence alive while a case moves through the courts.

A tip, a fence, and a criminal case 

Environmental journalist Tony Carnie got an anonymous tip about the trees, photographed them through a fence at the Africa Global Logistics warehouse in Durban’s Mobeni industrial area, and reported the seizure in Daily Maverick in October . AGL told the publication it only provided logistics services and neither owned nor exported the cargo.

Every baobab in South Africa is a specially protected species under the National…
items.t: South Africa seized 5 ancient baobabs bound for Georgia, where 8 Kenyan trees died in a billionaire’s park

items.title: To appoint the next comptroller general of the United States, follow the law
items.summary:
The new approach being employed to appoint the next Comptroller General of the United States should raise a red flag. The Government Accountability Office (GAO), which is headed by the Comptroller General, plays an important role in helping Congress discharge its responsibilities under Article I of the U.S. Constitution, particularly in connection with oversight of the Executive Branch.

We were shocked to learn that U.S. Sen. Rand Paul (R-KY), Chairman of the Senate Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs (HSGAC), recently and spontaneously requested that names be submitted to him, under a short time constraint, to be recommended to the President for nomination as the next Comptroller General of the United States.

Under the GAO Act of 1980, a 10-member statutory bipartisan and bicameral Comptroller General Selection Commission was created. Chairman Paul is a member, since he is Chair of the HSGAC, but he is not the Chairman of the Commission. That Commission is required to jointly develop and transmit a list of at least three qualified nominees to the President. That is the law, and that is how the process of appointing the Comptroller General has been conducted since 1980.

The current vacancy for Comptroller General of the United States began on Dec. 30, 2025, and yet the Commission and its members have never met.

Equally shocking is that Sen. Paul took the liberty as HSGAC Chairman to insert an empty placeholder for an unnamed nominee for Comptroller General of the United States for a Nov. 19, 2026, Committee confirmation hearing.

Again, Sen. Paul…
items.t: To appoint the next comptroller general of the United States, follow the law

items.title: Craigslist founder Craig Newmark has given away $500M. He hopes the midterms were ‘the beginning of the end’ for big money in politics
items.summary:
Craig Newmark , who founded Craigslist in 1995, has given away more than $500 million, with some of that money going toward protecting American elections— and pigeons . Now Newmark is hoping the 2026 midterms mark a turning point for big money in politics.

Asked what Elon Musk’s midterm spending says about the limits of big money, Newmark said Tuesday at the Fortune 500 Innovation Forum in Detroit that he wants to see it as “the beginning of the end of the influence of really big money.”

“That may or may not be realistic,” added Newmark, who signed the Giving Pledge late last year. “We won’t know for another 10 years or more.”

Musk spent roughly half a billion dollars on the midterms and had little to show for it , considering most of his donations went to Republicans. Historically, money usually wins . In 2020, the top-spending House candidate won about 88% of the time .

Newmark said he has stepped back from trying to influence Washington himself. 

“I just decided that for myself, Washington politics is no country for old nerds,” he told Fortune Editorial Director Kristin Stoller, who moderated the panel. “My prior efforts have all failed, with the exception of where I chat with the people on the front lines of fighting off attacks from our foreign adversaries.” Even there, he said, “I’ve been told to keep my mouth shut.”

The foundation lists voter protection among its priorities, and election security and fighting disinformation have also been focuses of his giving. Just last week, he made a five-year, $28 million pledge to the Bob Woodruff Foundation .

‘I’m the…
items.t: Craigslist founder Craig Newmark has given away $500M. He hopes the midterms were ‘the beginning of the end’ for big money in politics

items.title: ‘I’m not afraid of Chinese cars’: GM’s president says Detroit will be the bastion of American manufacturing as China breaks auto export records
items.summary:
General Motors President Mark Reuss wanted to make one thing clear at the F500 Innovation Forum in Detroit: “I’m not afraid of Chinese cars.” At the same time, he said GM is taking China’s growing automotive manufacturing industry “very seriously.” China exported more than 8 million passenger vehicles in the first 10 months of 2026, and Reuss’ answer is to point to Detroit’s GM’s factories.

Reuss spoke during a panel discussion with Fortune ’s Executive Editor Lee Clifford. “I think we do a lot of things really well,” he said. “Core things like safety, durability, reliability, long term, and of course design—aesthetic design.”

And the stakes are American jobs: the motor vehicles and component parts sector employed about 2.6 million U.S. workers in 2025, according to the Department of Energy , a drop of more than 50,000 from the year before. But he pointed to GM’s factories, production scale and workforce as competitive advantages that Chinese competitors can’t replicate.

“I think Detroit is doing a lot of things well,” he said. “We look at our factories and our scale, and we do scale well.”

He also pointed to GM’s people. “I think our talent is second to none. I really do,” Reuss said. “We have the best talent in this country in automotive, I believe.”

And one of the ways they were doing it? He said the company had been operating in China since 1984—studying its competitor: “We know Chinese cars,” Reuss said.

And GM still takes apart rivals’ cars from around the world to see what competitors are doing, Reuss said. “Only the paranoid survive, right?”

China is turning…
items.t: ‘I’m not afraid of Chinese cars’: GM’s president says Detroit will be the bastion of American manufacturing as China breaks auto export records

items.title: Nvidia’s interim CEO Colette Kress takes on export compliance as Washington turns up pressure
items.summary:
Nvidia’s national security and trade compliance teams will report directly to interim CEO Colette Kress and a new board oversight committee on day-to-day operations as the AI giant faces heightened scrutiny from Washington. Compliance has become a critical issue for Nvidia and for Kress, who is also the company’s longtime finance chief, as questions swirl over the potential diversion of its advanced AI to China.

The company said Tuesday that its board has formed a National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee to oversee national security policies, export-control compliance and global trade risks. Suzanne Nora Johnson will chair the panel, joined by directors Stephen C. Neal and John O. Dabiri. The committee will meet at least quarterly and work with independent experts.

Board Chair Harvey Jones said the committee would work to establish and advance a robust framework to “safeguard national security while supporting continued technological innovation.”

The move comes amid heightened U.S. scrutiny of access to advanced AI chips. The Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security announced Monday an interim final rule addressing remote access to advanced computing technology through overseas data centers. The rule, developed at the direction of the Treasury Department and the National Security Council, aims to prevent companies in restricted countries from bypassing export controls by accessing computing power remotely through data centers in third countries.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has publicly criticized Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick over…
items.t: Nvidia’s interim CEO Colette Kress takes on export compliance as Washington turns up pressure

items.title: SBA chief defends policy barring green-card holders from loans, even if they can serve in U.S. military
items.summary:
Small Business Administration chief Kelly Loeffler said Tuesday it’s “completely not true” that her agency’s new loan rules restrict immigrants. The rules she was defending bar green-card holders, who can legally work, pay taxes and, if otherwise eligible, enlist in the U.S. military, from SBA-backed loans.

Under a policy that took effect March 1 , businesses must be wholly owned by U.S. citizens or nationals to qualify for SBA-backed loans, cutting out lawful permanent residents, commonly known as green-card holders, who were previously eligible. In fiscal 2025, the agency approved 3,358 loans to businesses partly owned by lawful permanent residents, about 4% of its 85,000 loan approvals, according to the SBA . Speaking at the Fortune 500 Innovation Forum in Detroit, Loeffler cast the rule as a question of who goes first: “Foreign nationals cannot get an SBA loan ahead of an American citizen.”

“It strikes me as odd that we can send somebody to a battlefield on behalf of the United States,” Fortune Brainstorm Editorial Director Andrew Nusca told Loeffler. “We can take their taxes, but we can’t extend to them a loan.”

“We have not yet run into a case where we’ve had to reject a veteran for that purpose,” Loeffler said. She didn’t directly address why green-card holders who serve in the military should be excluded. Instead, she pointed to the agency’s work supporting veterans, including a policy waiving down payments for eligible veteran entrepreneurs.

Loeffler also argued that the SBA has limited funding and accounts for only a small share of the broader small-business…
items.t: SBA chief defends policy barring green-card holders from loans, even if they can serve in U.S. military

items.title: ‘Both utopians and the doomers are going to be disappointed’: Fed advisor Marc Andreessen on AI going from boom to bust
items.summary:
Marc Andreessen got the last word at the Federal Reserve’s big AI conference in San Francisco on Monday, and he used it to tell the central bank that nearly everyone in the room was going to be let down.

“My line has been both utopians and the doomers are going to be disappointed,” the venture capitalist said at the San Francisco Fed , “specifically disappointed by the scope and magnitude of the real-world impact, and specifically the economic impact.”

Andreessen co-leads the Productivity and Jobs Task Force, which Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh set up to tell the central bank what super intelligence—“SI,” in the White House’s preferred term—will do to growth, prices and jobs. On Monday, Andreessen previewed what he’ll contribute to the group’s report. Without using the name, he described one of the oldest problems in economics: William Baumol’s “cost disease,” the reason flat-screen TVs get cheaper every year while hospital bills, tuition and rent go the other way. His case is that AI won’t cure it, and could even make it worse.

The Fed hasn’t quite laid out that outcome.

The task force is advisory, and Andreessen has no vote on interest rates. He co-leads it with Stanford economist Charles Jones and Microsoft executive Asha Sharma, one of five outside panels the Fed named in June to rethink how the central bank works. Its charge, per the Fed , is to assess the economic impact of “new general-purpose technologies, including super intelligence, to inform the Federal Reserve’s policy judgments.” The panels report to the rate-setting committee with recommendations due by…
items.t: ‘Both utopians and the doomers are going to be disappointed’: Fed advisor Marc Andreessen on AI going from boom to bust

items.title: The Fed’s first close look at the AI buildout finds $3 trillion of AI commitments that aren’t on big tech’s balance sheet as debt
items.summary:
The first time the Federal Reserve took a close look at how the AI buildout is being financed, it found more than $3 trillion of promises that don’t show up as debt.

The Fed’s November Financial Stability Report includes a new section, “Leverage in the Data Center Buildout.” None of the report’s five previous editions, going back to 2024, had one. The closest, in November 2025, was about AI and algorithmic trading.

The new section counts more than $1 trillion in leases that are signed but haven’t started yet, plus more than $2 trillion in take-or-pay contracts and residual value guarantees, at Amazon , Alphabet , Broadcom , Meta , Microsoft , Nvidia , and Oracle . 

Citing the report in a speech Monday in Milan, Fed Governor Michael Barr put the “potential maximum nominal value” of those obligations above $3 trillion. He said the seven largest AI firms’ on-balance-sheet debt “is expected to exceed $800 billion before year’s end.” The Fed notes the off-balance-sheet figures are undiscounted and “not directly comparable” with debt. 

Amazon, Alphabet, Broadcom, Meta, Microsoft, and Oracle didn’t immediately respond to Fortune ’s requests for comment.

Debt, not-yet-started leases, and guarantees and contract commitments at Amazon, Alphabet, Broadcom, Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia and Oracle, through the second quarter of 2026. items.title: The man who sold Aetna to CVS for almost $70 billion says the deal was cover for problems ‘they never really fixed’—just as CVS breaks itself in two
items.summary:
Mark Bertolini sold Aetna to CVS Health for almost $70 billion in 2018. On Monday, he told a room of Fortune 500 executives what he thinks CVS was really buying.

“The real intention” of the purchase, Bertolini said at the Fortune 500 Innovation Forum in Detroit, “was just to take the earning stream and revenue stream from [Aetna] to hide a bunch of other things that they never really fixed.” He tied that directly to the breakup CVS is going through now: “You’d never do that deal now.”

The comments land two weeks after CVS said it will split in two . CVS Health will keep Aetna and its Caremark pharmacy benefit manager and spin off its roughly 9,000 stores and MinuteClinic as a separate company, CVS Pharmacy, by the first half of 2028. CVS shares closed down 12.5% on Nov. 4, the day of the announcement, wiping out nearly $15 billion in market value. 

For employers, insurers, and anyone with a pharmacy benefit, it’s the partial unwinding of the biggest bet on vertical integration in American health care.

CVS declined to comment on Bertolini’s remarks. “This is the right decision, at the right time,” CVS Health spokesperson David Whitrap said of the split in an email to Fortune, adding that the company is “getting ahead of the external market dynamics from a position of strength. Each of our businesses are thriving.” He confirmed that Aetna and Caremark will stay together and that the separation should be finished by mid-2028.

Where’s the queen? 

Bertolini ran Aetna from 2011 through the sale and has been CEO of Oscar Health since April 2023. He had been asked by Fortune…
items.t: The man who sold Aetna to CVS for almost $70 billion says the deal was cover for problems ‘they never really fixed’—just as CVS breaks itself in two

items.title: Anthropic recognises the risks to humanity – but is its governance really up to the job? | Nils Pratley
items.summary:
The Claude AI developer’s unique setup is supposedly high-minded, but still represents extraordinary power concentration

Boardroom governance matters, even in the world of big tech, it turns out. The business of how companies are run, investors are discovering, can be more complicated than handing the founder or superstar chief executive as much control as he wants (it’s usually a he) and waiting for brilliant returns to appear. Sometimes a few checks on power are useful, especially when a crisis strikes.

This revelation is no revelation at all, of course. For about 30 years until the first generation of big US tech companies came along, the thrust of corporate governance thinking was to insist on the basic fairness of the principle of “one share, one vote”. The owners should be able to chuck out misbehaving or underperforming managers by a simple majority, in other words.

items.t: Anthropic recognises the risks to humanity – but is its governance really up to the job?

items.title: At 17, South Carolina-bound GG Banks is building a brand before her first college game
items.summary:
Jezelle “GG” Banks doesn’t turn 18 until Nov. 27, but she already has a logo.

The senior at The St. James Academy, just outside Washington, D.C., is a five-star guard ranked No. 4 in the class of 2027 and committed to South Carolina, the No. 1 team in the AP poll. She’s as at home slicing past defenders as she is hosting long livestreams on social media.

Banks is also building a business. In a growing number of states, high school athletes can now be paid for their name, image, and likeness (NIL), just like college athletes. In an exclusive interview with Fortune , she revealed her personal logo publicly for the first time.

“I love it! It really fits me,” Banks said. “Everything in the logo has special meaning to me. I think the logo speaks to my personality—spikes of energy boosting everything, and then towards the bottom you’ve got a dollar sign, because, of course, banks.”

Logo Design & Branding: THE·TEAM 

The dollar sign plays on her last name. Banks worked on the design with her agency, THE·TEAM , the sports and entertainment firm formerly known as Wasserman. Coming just weeks before her 18th birthday, it’s a birthday present of sorts.

“This was a dream,” Banks said. THE·TEAM showed her mockups of the logo on sneakers and in Times Square. “That’s what I envisioned when I was younger, me having the logo.”

Building who she was on the court 

Custom logos are still rare among high school players, but Banks has been dreaming big for a while.

“I saw this coming a little bit, not just for me, but I think just the women’s era—people paying more attention to women’s…
items.t: At 17, South Carolina-bound GG Banks is building a brand before her first college game
